pages: Day 119: Not all of them die. I did not know that. Some we leave behind, and they are still there in the morning, standing in the ash with their hands at their sides, weeping. They do not see us. They do not see anything.

At sunrise they are gone. Not dead, not walked away. Gone, like breath off a window. At dusk they stand in the same places again. His men will not go near them. He says they are what the corruption leaves behind when the body is burned too late.

One of the villagers, before he turned, told me the bell would send them home. I rang it. It was the only thing that still rang in that whole village. They went still, all of them, and lifted their faces, and then there was nothing standing there but smoke. I have not told Him.
